Option 2: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences. Call record_choice for the one to keep. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself. It works by breaking a large task down into smaller, identical versions of the original task. To prevent the function from looping infinitely, it must include a stopping condition known as a base case. When the base case is finally reached, the results from all the smaller tasks bubble back up to form the final solution.
